notes.title: KEYBOARD INPUT DETAILED
notes.notes:
We’re constantly working to improve 198X. By player request, we’ve now added keyboard input specifications for each arcade game, accessible through the pause menu. Hope they help! 

We’ve also eliminated quite a few bugs, rendering 198X a better playing game overall.

As always: thanks for your continued support in spreading the word of 198X. Without you, we wouldn't be here.

notes.title: ACHIEVEMENTS GET!
notes.notes:
By popular demand, we’ve now added Steam Achievements to 198X! Can you unlock all 14? 

We’ve also squashed some pesky bugs – and added the option to view the end credits at will after having completed the game. 

From all of us in the 198X team: thanks for your kind support and overwhelmingly positive feedback since launch.

notes.title: 198X offers solace for the arcade generation today
notes.notes:
Arcade teen dramaventure 198X is out today, or at least its first chapter is. Developers Hi-Bit Studios call it “a coming-of-age story told through multiple games and genres”. What that means is five loosely connected arcade games channelling Outrun, R-Type, Final Fight and Ninja Spirit, plus a dungeon-crawling RPG, all in the service of a larger story. While I still say the sprites are more ’90s than ’80s (but won’t get bogged down in that argument again), I can’t deny that they are gorgeous looking, both within the games and during the story vignettes.
